2_Introduction: The PSCs exhibited a superior PCE of 22.585% (JSC: 26.057 mA/cm², VOC: 1.1027 V, FF: 78.6013%). The precursor solutions for all Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0 films were prepared by dissolving equimolar concentrations (1.73 mol/L). The film was deposited under controlled conditions, involving an initial spin of 1000 rpm (5 s) followed by a second spin at 5500 rpm (30 s). During the last 15 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (150 µL of chlorobenzene) was dropped in the center at a constant rate Subsequently, the as-deposited films were annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₈FA₀.₈₇PbI₃.₀ perovskite films—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibit enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic tolerance factor optimization (t ≈ 0.92) conferred by the co-incorporation of small-radius Cs⁺, intermediate-size MA⁺, and large-radius FA⁺, which collectively suppresses octahedral tilting, mitigates lattice strain, and reduces thermodynamic driving forces for ion migration; this compositional design, combined with precisely controlled crystallization kinetics—initiated by low-speed nucleation at 1000 rpm to promote uniform precursor wetting, followed by rapid shear-driven dewetting and supersaturation at 5500 rpm—enables homogeneous nucleation density, while the timed, centripetal antisolvent quenching (150 µL chlorobenzene delivered during the final 15 s of high-speed spin) selectively extracts DMSO to arrest intermediate solvate phases before uncontrolled aggregation, yielding dense, pinhole-free morphologies with minimal grain boundary area and suppressed non-radiative recombination centers; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the stoichiometric equimolar precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L), which avoids PbI₂-rich or organic-halide-deficient intermediates, and the optimized thermal annealing (110 °C, 15 min) fully volatilizes residual solvent while completing crystallographic ordering without inducing decomposition—evidenced by XRD patterns showing sharp, intense (110) and (220) perovskite peaks with narrow FWHM (<0.12°) and complete absence of residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°), confirming quantitative conversion and low microstrain; optical characterization further corroborates this structural fidelity, as uniform PL intensity mapping reveals spatially homogeneous radiative recombination across the film with negligible dark spots, indicating near-complete surface coverage and suppressed trap-assisted recombination, while time-resolved PL decays exhibit monoexponential kinetics with extended carrier lifetimes (>1.2 µs), directly linking the optimized crystallization pathway to reduced deep-level defects and efficient charge extraction—ultimately enabling VOC of 1.1027 V, JSC of 26.057 mA/cm², FF of 78.6013%, and PCE of 22.585%.
